title.narrative: Stabilization and Recovery in Eastern DRC

description.narrative: The Project Development Objective is to (i) improve access to community infrastructure; (ii) enhance the socio-economic reintegration and resilience of individuals affected by conflict; and (iii) strengthen the capacity of the administrations in Selected Provinces.

The development objective of Stabilization and Recovery in Eastern DRC Project for Democratic Republic of Congo is to: (i) improve access to community infrastructure; (ii) enhance the socioeconomic reintegration and resilience of individuals affected by conflict; and (iii) strengthen the capacity of the administrations in selected provinces. This project has five components. 1) The first component, Community-based stabilization, has following sub-components: (i) Facilitation and capacity building for community participatory planning; and (ii) Investments in social and economic climate resilient community infrastructure. 2) The second component, Community-based Reintegration, has the following sub-components: (i) Labor-intensive public works (LIPW); (ii) Cash grants for income-generating activities (IGAs); and (iii) Psycho-social support. 3) The third component, Decentralized Governance, finances the necessary government institutions and systems to enhance ways in which government and external partner resources can be used to sustain medium term stabilization and recovery. 4) The fourth component, Project Management and Research, has the following sub-components: (i) Project Management; (ii) Technical Assistance; and (iii) Research and Learning. 5) The fifth component, Contingency Emergency Response (CERC), aims to establish a disaster contingency fund that may be triggered in the event of a of a national emergency such as COVID-19.

condition.narrative: For purposes of providing LIPW, IGA Grants and psycho-social support under Component 2 of the Project, the Recipient shall ensure,throughout Project implementation, that the pertinent targeted armed group which the corresponding P-DDRCS Participant's individualformed part, has been voluntarily disarmed, following the Recipient's rules, eligibility criteria and implementation process, andas determined in collaboration with MONUSCO; as further described in the PIM.

Section I.A. 3 of Schedule 2: The Recipient shall, no later than five (5) months after the Effective Date, or such other date asagreed by the Association, cause each of the Selected Provinces to, establish and thereafter maintain a provincial consultationcommittee (“Provincial Consultation Committee”) with terms of reference, composition and powers acceptable to the Association anddefined in the PIM.

Section I.A.1 of schedule 2: The Recipient shall cause each of the Recipient's provinces of Ituri, Nord Kivu and South Kivu to, nolater than three (3) months after the Effective Date, or such other date as agreed by the Association, but in any case prior to theimplementation of any activity under their respective administrative jurisdiction, establish by provincial arrêtE, an thereaftermaintain, throughout Project implementation, a civilian implementation support unit in Bunia, Goma, and Bukavu.

Section I.A.2 of Schedule 2: The Recipient shall, no later than three (3) months after the Effective Date, or such later date asagreed by the Association, establish and thereafter maintain throughout Project implementation, a Project operational steeringcommittee (“Steering Committee”), chaired by the Governors of the Selected Provinces (on an annual rotating basis).

Section I.A.6 of Schedule 2 on the TPM: No later than three (3) months after the Effective Date, or such other date as agreed bythe Association, the Recipient shall cause the Coordination Provinciale of Nord Kivu, in coordination with the CoordinationGEnErale, to : (a) select and hire a third party monitoring firm (“TPM Consultant”) with terms of reference, qualifications andexperience satisfactory to the Association to monitor the implementation of the Project in accordance with the provisions of thisAgreement (including the environmental and social measures and actions included in the ESCP).

Section I.G of Schedule 2 on the Use of Military and Security Actors: 1. All activities activities under the Project shall be underthe control of the Recipient's civil authorities and shall be undertaken exclusively for the purposes related to the Project. Allgoods, works, services, Operating Costs, and Training financed by the Financing proceeds shall be used under the direction andcontrol of the Recipient's civil authorities and strictly in accordance with the PIM and this Agreement. 2. In the event thatduring Project implementation the military or security personnel is engaged in the generation of any assets, procurement of goodsand/or construction of works financed out of the Financing proceeds, and except as the Association may otherwise agree, theRecipient shall ensure that that the ownership of said assets generated, goods procured, and works constructed by the military orsecurity personnel shall be transferred to, or shall vest, with the Recipient's civil authorities at provincial and local levels,as applicable, and agreed with the Association.
